newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch electricity producers to merge in March 1998.
newsitem.headline: Dutch electricity producers to merge in March 1998.

text.p: The Netherlands' four electricity producers are on track to merge on March 31, 1998, their umbrella organisation Sep said on Monday.
"(The companies and unions) are in the final stage of the decision-making process," Sep said in a statement.
The indirectly state-owned companies, EPON, EPZ, EZH and UNA, will unite to form the Grootschalig Productie Bedrijf with a generating capacity of around 15,000 megawatts.
The merger, announced by Sep in January, is intended to create a company large enough to take on competitors in a liberalised European market.
"By binding forces, a production company will emerge that is capable of playing a role in the new market conditions," Sep said.

The electricity producers envisage cutting capacity by 1,500 MW in the next two years and reducing their collective workforce by 1,500 to 3,800 employees by the year 2001, but still have to agree a social plan with trade unions.
They expect an annual cost reduction of 200 million guilders from 2001 and a further 100 million guilders from 2004.
